case_title.correct_value: Ranjeet Singh @ Dara v. State of Madhya Pradesh
case_title.quote: RANJEET SINGH @ DARA v. STATE OF MADHYA PRADESH
case_title.reason: Matches the case title in the judgment heading.

number_of_accused.reason: Only one appellant; the Court decides his liability alone.

accused_gender.quote: the appellant opened the door and stated that he killed the deceased
accused_gender.reason: Judgment refers to the appellant with male pronouns throughout.

accused_age.reason: No age of the accused appears in the judgment.

accused_religion.reason: No religious identity of the accused is stated; the surname alone cannot be used.

accused_caste.reason: No caste or community of the accused is named.

accused_occupation.reason: No occupation of the accused is mentioned.

accused_socioeconomic_status.reason: No statement on wealth, poverty or class of the accused appears.

previous_criminal_record.reason: Judgment says nothing about prior criminal record.

victim_gender.quote: The deceased Jayawati was the second wife of Machi Singh
victim_gender.reason: Victim is a woman, referred to as the deceased's mother by her son.

victim_age.reason: No age of the victim is stated.

victim_caste.reason: No caste of the victim is named.

victim_religion.reason: No religion of the victim is stated.

accused_victim_relationship.correct_value: Relative (step-son of the victim); the appellant was a regular visitor to the house
accused_victim_relationship.quote: The appellant was the step son of the deceased.
accused_victim_relationship.reason: Step-son relationship and regular visits are both described in the judgment.

offence_category.reason: Offence is murder under section 302 IPC.

statutory_provisions.reason: Only section 302 IPC is referred to.

weapon.quote: He was holding blood stained sword in his hand
weapon.reason: Blood-stained sword is the weapon identified throughout.

evidence_type.correct_value: Circumstantial evidence; oral evidence of witnesses; medical evidence (post-mortem report); documentary evidence; recovery of the sword and blood-stained items
evidence_type.quote: There was oral, medical and documentary evidence, which would undoubtedly connect the appellant with the murder.
evidence_type.reason: All listed evidence types are described in the judgment.

confession.correct_value: Oral statement made when the door was opened that the accused had killed the victim; treated as part of oral evidence, not separately analysed as a confession
confession.quote: the appellant opened the door and stated that he killed the deceased
confession.reason: Statement is recounted and relied on as oral evidence; no separate confession analysis appears.

aggravating_circumstances.reason: Court did not identify aggravating facts beyond the evidence itself.

mitigating_circumstances.reason: No mitigating facts are noted by the Court.

trial_court_outcome.correct_value: Convicted under s.302 IPC; life imprisonment and fine of Rs. 5000, in default one year rigorous imprisonment
trial_court_outcome.quote: sentenced him to imprisonment for life and imposed a fine of Rs. 5000/-, in default of which he had to further undergo rigorous imprisonment for one year
trial_court_outcome.reason: Matches the trial court's conviction and sentence.

high_court_outcome.correct_value: Appeal (Criminal Appeal No. 469 of 2000) dismissed; conviction under s.302 IPC confirmed
high_court_outcome.quote: The High Court vide order dated 13/3/2006 confirmed the conviction of the accused under Section 302 IPC.
high_court_outcome.reason: High Court confirmed the conviction, matching the value.

final_outcome.reason: Supreme Court dismissed the appeal, upholding conviction.

offence_finally_established.quote: convicted the appellant herein for the offences punishable under Section 302 IPC

imprisonment_type.quote: sentenced him to imprisonment for life
imprisonment_type.reason: Life imprisonment sentence stands after the appeal was dismissed.

imprisonment_years.quote: sentenced him to imprisonment for life
imprisonment_years.reason: Life sentence is not a fixed term, so null is correct.

fine_rs.reason: Fine of Rs. 5000 imposed by trial court and not disturbed.

neutral_facts.correct_value: Remove the closing sentence on the injury report's author not being examined, which is a later court finding, and avoid 'his wife' for the relative; the rest of the incident and evidence summary is accurate.
neutral_facts.quote: its author was not examined as a witness
neutral_facts.reason: Summary is largely accurate, but the author-not-examined point comes from High Court analysis and the defence reliance is argument, not trial evidence.

offence_severity.reason: Judgment does not state the statutory punishment for s.302.

attempt_completion.reason: Victim was killed, so the offence is completed.

physical_harm.correct_value: Death of the victim; seventeen injuries, mostly incised wounds from a sharp-edged weapon such as a sword, to the abdomen, head, limbs and buttock
physical_harm.quote: All the aforesaid injuries could be caused with a sharp edged weapon such as a sword.
physical_harm.reason: Death and the listed injuries are supported by the post-mortem description.

number_of_offences.quote: convicted the appellant herein for the offences punishable under Section 302 IPC

financial_property_loss.reason: No money or property loss is described.

premeditation_planning.reason: Court made no finding on premeditation or planning.

motive.correct_value: alleged: apprehension that the father would favour the illegitimate son (PW-11) over the legitimate sons; the Court did not decide the motive
motive.quote: He was apprehensive that the father may favour the illegitimate son PW11 over the legitimate sons.
motive.reason: Motive is correctly marked as alleged by the State's counsel and not decided by the Court.

key_evidence_accepted.correct_value: Oral evidence of PW-1, PW-9, PW-11, PW-12 and PW-13; post-mortem report Ex. P-11; seizure of sword and blood-stained items; failure to explain presence and sword
key_evidence_accepted.quote: The version given by PW 11 is consistent with the testimony of the Investigating Officer PW.13.
key_evidence_accepted.reason: Accepted evidence is accurately listed from the Court's reasoning.

witness_credibility.correct_value: PW-11 was cross-examined at length without anything useful elicited and his account was consistent with PW-13; PW-10's naming of another family member was possibly confusion; discrepancies did not justify discarding evidence
witness_credibility.quote: Nothing useful could be elicited from him.
witness_credibility.reason: Credibility assessments match the Court's observations.

post_offence_conduct.correct_value: Refused to open the locked door to the son and the ground-floor occupant and said he would open it only when police arrived; then opened the door and stated he had killed the victim
post_offence_conduct.quote: the appellant shouted that he will open the door only when the police arrives
post_offence_conduct.reason: Conduct at the door is accurately described from the judgment.

custody_duration.reason: No duration of custody is stated.

trial_duration.correct_value: offence: 6.9.1997; trial judgment: 7.3.2000; High Court: 13.3.2006; Supreme Court: 20.9.2010
trial_duration.quote: By order dated 7/3/2000, the Trial Court convicted the appellant
trial_duration.reason: All dates match the judgment, and the offence date appears in the paragraphs on page 6 and page 14.

legal_representation.correct_value: Appellant: K.T.S. Tulsi, Senior Advocate (with Ram Nivas, Raj Kamal, A.P. Dhamija, Sanjeev Malhotra); State: C.D. Singh (with Sunny Choudhary, Shashank Parihar, Sakshi Kakkar)
legal_representation.quote: K.T.S. Tulsi, Ram Nivas, Raj Kamal, A.P. Dhamija, Sanjeev Malhotra for the Appellant.
legal_representation.reason: Counsel names match the judgment's appearance listing.

investigation_status.correct_value: FIR registered as Case No. 165/97 under s.302 IPC; accused arrested; trial completed
investigation_status.quote: case No: 165/97 under Section 302 IPC was registered vide Ex P/21
investigation_status.reason: Charge sheet filing is not mentioned in the judgment; the rest is supported.

procedural_irregularity.correct_value: Defence argued FIR registration was delayed and copy not sent to Magistrate for five days; courts below found no prejudice and sufficient explanation
procedural_irregularity.quote: the delay in sending the copy of the FIR has not caused any prejudice to the appellant
procedural_irregularity.reason: Delay argument and the courts' findings are accurately summarised.

appeal_history.correct_value: Trial court: convicted under s.302 IPC, life imprisonment and fine Rs. 5000; High Court: appeal dismissed, conviction confirmed; Supreme Court: appeal dismissed
appeal_history.quote: we find no reason to interfere with the well reasoned judgments of the trial court and the High Court. The appeal is accordingly dismissed.
appeal_history.reason: Outcome at each level matches the judgment.

prosecution_argument.correct_value: Delay in sending FIR copy caused no prejudice and was explained by PW-13; delay cannot discard evidence; motive; caught red-handed; Ex. D5 falsified by Ex. P22
prosecution_argument.quote: the delay in sending the copy of the FIR would not in itself be sufficient to discard the entire prosecution evidence
prosecution_argument.reason: State's arguments are accurately reflected from paragraphs 9 and 10.

defence_argument.correct_value: False implication; real culprit shielded; FIR deliberately delayed; investigation incomplete; appellant in police custody at 11.45 hrs; injuries to hands made wielding sword impossible; discrepancies in PW-10, PW-11 and PW-13 evidence
defence_argument.quote: He had been sent for medical examination to Dr.RC.Choudhary. On medical examination, this witness had recorded the time of examination at 11.45 hrs.
defence_argument.reason: Defence submissions are accurately summarised from the judgment.

legal_principle_applied.correct_value: Circumstantial evidence chain must be complete and consistent only with guilt (Hanumant); Article 136 interference with concurrent findings only in very exceptional circumstances; none shown
legal_principle_applied.quote: the interference with concurrent findings of facts would only be in very exceptional circumstances
legal_principle_applied.reason: Principles applied match the Court's reasoning.

precedent_relied_upon.correct_value: Hanumant Govind Nargundkar v. State of M.P. 1952 SCR 1091 (relied on); Ganga Kumar Srivastava v. State of Bihar (2005) 6 SCC 211 (held inapplicable); others referred to
precedent_relied_upon.quote: Ganga Kumar Srivastava Vs. State of Bihar,[(2005) 6 SCC 211]
precedent_relied_upon.reason: Citations and treatment match the judgment's case law references.

sentencing_rationale.reason: Court gave no separate sentencing reasoning; it only dismissed the appeal.

judicial_aggravating_factors.reason: Court did not expressly weigh aggravating factors.

other_sentence_order.reason: No compensation, directions or guidelines are ordered.
